reason: Both answers fully satisfy the request with sound, distinct critiques—confounding, selection/reverse causation, exposure and denominator problems, ecological aggregation, spillovers, and limited external validity—and both propose a credible staggered, preferably randomized rollout with before/after comparisons, exposure measures, spillover monitoring, and attention to rare outcomes and heterogeneous effects. A usefully adds empirical-Bayes adjustment and regression discontinuity; B usefully adds an eligible-corridor sampling frame, geocoded segment-level outcomes, and explicit power planning. These are complementary strengths rather than a meaningful difference in overall correctness or usefulness.
